spain.title: How to Buy a Co-Ownership Share in Spain (2026 Guide)
spain.h1: How to buy a co-ownership share in Spain
spain.subtitle: The structure, the NIE, the taxes you do and do not pay, what it costs measured across the 82 Spanish homes we list, and the seven steps in the order they happen.
spain.metaDescription: You buy a share in a Spanish SL, so no transfer tax on it. You need an NIE, which takes four to eight weeks. 82 homes from €120,000, four operators.

france.title: How to Buy a Co-Ownership Share in France (2026 Guide)
france.h1: How to buy a co-ownership share in France
france.subtitle: The SCI, the notaire fees you avoid, how IFI works for residents and non-residents, what it costs across the 22 French homes we list, and the steps in order.
france.metaDescription: You buy a share in a French SCI, so the 7.5–8% notaire transfer duties do not apply. IFI rarely bites on one share. 22 homes from €119,000.

italy.title: How to Buy a Co-Ownership Share in Italy (2026 Guide)
italy.h1: How to buy a co-ownership share in Italy
italy.subtitle: The SRL, who actually pays IMU, the codice fiscale, what it costs across the 23 Italian homes we list — the lowest running costs of any country we cover.
italy.metaDescription: You buy a share in an Italian SRL, so no imposta di registro. IMU is paid by the company. 23 homes from €119,000 and the lowest running costs.

usa.title: How to Buy a Co-Ownership Share in the USA (2026)
usa.h1: How to buy a co-ownership share in the United States
usa.subtitle: The property-specific LLC, what the US market does better and worse than Europe, what it costs across the 107 American homes we list, and the steps in order.
usa.metaDescription: You buy a share in a property-specific LLC. 107 homes across 11 states from $68,000, Pacaso’s uncapped nights, and why letting is not allowed here.
